skill: trailofbits/skills plugins/audit-context-building (pinned); run as a subagent writing one record per function to review/context/functions/ (storage__*, core__Vault__Secret_Guard__*, core__Vault__Ignore__*; 60 records)
run: 2026-10-11; the dossier names no vulnerabilities by design. The records below are its `nothing found` assumptions and open questions turned into claims to verify in step 4; the hunting is the agent's, the evidence is the dossier's

findings.title: Safe_Str__Vault_Path rewrites every character outside [a-zA-Z0-9/\_.- ] to '_', so a vault root with '~', ':', '+', '@', ',' or any non-ASCII letter splits the store: object, ref, key and reflog paths resolve under the sanitised root while Vault__Storage, Components.sg_dir and the working copy use the raw one
evidence: Safe_Str__Vault_Path: regex REPLACE mode, no strict validation
Vault__Object_Store.object_path L96-97, Vault__Ref_Manager._ref_path, Vault__Key_Manager._key_path L73, Vault__Reflog build under vault_path (the field typed Safe_Str__Vault_Path)
Vault__Storage.*(directory) and the working copy use the raw string
dossier: 'the one assumption underneath the whole storage layer with nothing enforcing it'
findings.impact: A6 / user: a vault in a home directory with a non-ASCII name keeps its ciphertext, refs and keys in a sibling path nobody expects; `uninit`'s secure_rmtree and backups operate on the raw path and leave them behind; two users whose roots sanitise to the same string share a store

proposed.fix: Safe_Str__Vault_Path must not rewrite: validate the root once at the boundary (raise on a root it cannot represent) or widen the character class to everything but NUL and path separators' odd forms; then a test that a vault at a path containing 'é', '+' and '@' round-trips (init, commit, status, uninit leaves nothing)
proposed.cost: S/M (type change touches every path field)

findings.title: fetch_tree_lazy writes host-named files under bare/data with plain open('wb'), no content-address check and no safe_join; it has no caller in sgit_ai but stays importable
findings.status: VERIFY (dead code; same class as TM-F01, reachable only by a future caller)
evidence: Vault__Sync__Base L626-629 and L649-653: os.path.join(sg_dir, 'bare', 'data', tree_id | fid.replace('bare/data/', '')) then open(..., 'wb')
grep sgit_ai: no caller of fetch_tree_lazy( outside its definition
Vault__Object_Store.store_at L74-82 (arbitrary write, force overwrite) likewise has no caller

proposed.fix: delete fetch_tree_lazy and store_at, or route them through Vault__Verified_Write.save; a test that no module-level write under bare/data bypasses Verified_Write (grep-as-test, like the eed8084 open() net)

findings.title: read_ref returns the decrypted 'commit_id' unvalidated (None, non-str, any string); it flows into Vault__Object_Store.load as a path component
evidence: read_ref L34-45: data.get('commit_id') after decrypt, no shape check
Object_Store.load L84-91: object_path(object_id) = join(vault_path, 'bare/data', id); a read-key holder (A3) who can write to the store authors ref contents (TM-R01), so the value is theirs

open(path, 'rb') reads only; a '../' commit_id reads a file outside bare/data and feeds its bytes to decrypt (which fails on anything not under the key); to check: whether any caller writes under a ref-derived id (Verified_Write.save is_store_path regex admits a trailing newline and '.'/'..' leaves per the dossier)

proposed.fix: read_ref validates commit_id against the object-id shape (obj-cas-imm-<12|32 hex>) and raises otherwise; is_store_path anchors with \Z and refuses '.'/'..' leaves
proposed.test: Known_Gaps or Fixed: a ref whose commit_id is '../../x' is refused at read, not at open

findings.title: readable() accepts `deleted: 1` for `deleted: true` (True == 1 in the round-trip compare), so an entry another client wrote that way is not carried but coerced
findings.status: VERIFY (low: coercion changes a tombstone's type, not its meaning)
evidence: readable L44-56: all(parsed[k] == v) with Python's True == 1

proposed.fix: compare with type(parsed[k]) is type(v) as well

findings.title: .gitignore is read with plain open(), not read_regular: a FIFO or a link at .gitignore blocks or redirects the scan (the eed8084 round closed this for every other working-copy read)
evidence: load_gitignore L76-85 plain open(); Vault__Repo_Ignore L53/L56 the same
rules can only exclude (never un-ignore ALWAYS_IGNORED or .env*), so the impact is availability (a FIFO hangs commit, TM-F27's class) or reading a file outside the tree as rules

proposed.test: a FIFO at .gitignore: commit refuses or skips with a warning, never hangs

findings.title: find_vault_root walks up to the nearest .sg_vault with no ceiling: a planted /tmp/.sg_vault or ~/.sg_vault (A6) captures every sgit command run below it
evidence: find_vault_root L86-96; CLI__Main L988-997 has no ceiling

git has the same behaviour (GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES exists for it); an A6 who can write /tmp/.sg_vault can plant a vault whose recorded server receives the user's next push (TM-F15/F22 pin the server per vault, which makes the planted vault's server authoritative)

proposed.fix: stop at the user's home directory boundary, or at a mount point, and name the root found on first use

findings.title: create_bare_structure (makedirs exist_ok) and secure_rmtree (isdir follows) assume .sg_vault itself is not a symlink planted before init / uninit
evidence: L69-81, L165-184; a pre-planted `.sg_vault -> /somewhere` (A6 with write access to the folder) makes init write keys there and uninit wipe there

proposed.fix: lstat .sg_vault before init and uninit; refuse a link

findings.title: check-then-open windows: safe_join checks the resolved path, then each caller opens with plain open(); secure_unlink checks islink then opens (TOCTOU for a local process racing the user)
findings.status: KNOWN (the threat model's A6 model accepts local races; read_regular closed the read side with O_NOFOLLOW)
evidence: safe_join L115-151 vs callers' open('wb'); secure_unlink L146-163
the write side has no O_NOFOLLOW equivalent for directories; the race needs a local attacker with write access to the working copy, who can already edit the files

findings.title: restore and init --restore rely on zipfile.extract's own stripping of '..' and absolute names, with no is_protected or link check on backup members
evidence: Vault__Restore._extract_bare L104, Vault__Sync__Lifecycle.restore_from_backup L159/L175 (comment says zipfile strips); TM-F03 says 'restore extracts store members only'; the dossier could not find the member-name allowlist on the lifecycle path
a backup is the user's own file, but a planted .vault__*.zip was TM-F03's vector

proposed.fix: extract only members matching Verified_Write.is_store_path or RESTORED_LOCAL_FILES, through safe_join

findings.title: push_state.json is written then chmod'ed (the pattern TM-F05 removed elsewhere); eight other local files use plain open() (remotes.json, merge state, cache, notices, reflog, stash, token store's base_url)
findings.status: VERIFY (low: none of these hold a key; base_url and remotes decide where keys go)
evidence: dossier list: Push L754-759, Remote_Manager L122, Merge__State L34, Cache_Manager L279, Vault__Ignore L169, Sync__Base L661, Reflog L42, Stash L67, Token_Store L160

proposed.fix: write_private for remotes.json and base_url (they route the token); leave the rest

findings.title: classify marks a non-content-addressed name under bare/data (an 'obj-<hex>' change-pack name) VERIFIED without any check
evidence: classify L43-66: VERIFIED iff not CAS or sha256 matches; a host serving bytes under a non-CAS data name passes containment only
to check: which paths accept such names from the host (change packs, bundles)

findings.title: _secret_entry fails open on BadZipFile / ValueError / RuntimeError and has no decompressed-size bound
findings.status: KNOWN (TM-R34: the guard is a last resort by design); the size bound is new
evidence: a zip bomb at a tracked path makes commit read it in full

proposed.fix: cap the bytes read per entry (the 64 KiB .pem rule exists; apply a total)
